text:
Anna (arch): Heads-up — saw routing flaps between hosted -> dedicated fallbacks this morning. Two requests ended up being served twice (one in hosted, one in dedicated).
Miguel: yikes. steps to repro?
Anna (arch): small spike, started at 09:07. path: client -> hosted gateway -> routing policy fallback -> dedicated pool. The gateway retried while dedicated accepted the same job.
Jeff: my suspicion: lease / dedup token TTL mismatch between the two pools. If hosted marks req as in-flight for 300ms and dedicated accepts after 250ms, gateway retry can race.
Sara: is this the same issue where private deployments don't surface lease state to control plane? we saw similar in air-gapped tests.
Anna (arch): yeah similar surface. In private mode the agent ACKs locally, control plane never learns. Fallbacks use control-plane view so they think hosted failed and reissue.
Rachel: two immediate approaches: (1) unify lease namespace across modes so preflight checks are consistent, or (2) add a preflight mutex/compare-and-swap on the gateway to avoid double-issue.
Miguel: option 2 sounds less invasive. but gateways are stateless proxies for hosted traffic — adding CAS is a change to the datapath.
Jeff: right. Option 1 requires private to publish a small opaque lease token to the gateway (not control plane) so gateway can short-circuit retries. But private deployments may refuse any extra network calls.
Sara: exact. Private customers explicitly disallow callouts. Any solution that relies on control plane visibility will break there.
Anna (arch): proposal 0: introduce a routing-lease token returned by runtime when it accepts; gateway stores token in short local cache keyed by request-id for TTL ~5s. If retry arrives and token present, gateway skips reissue. Minimal surface change, no control-plane dependency.
Rachel: that feels pragmatic. sketch of config:
```
routing: {
  retry_policy: { max_retries: 2, backoff_ms: 100 },
  local_lease_cache: { enabled: true, ttl_ms: 5000 }
}
```
Miguel: whoops — local_lease_cache on the gateway means memory pressure per instance. need LRU and bounded size.
Jeff: also need to consider cross-gateway duplicate if client retries to a different gateway. so this only prevents same-gateway double issue.
Anna (arch): correct. For cross-gateway duplicates we need a global namespace or a token client must pass back (idempotency key) that is validated by runtime. But clients are not always well-behaved.
Sara: alternative hybrid: gateway-local cache + runtime-generated idempotency token returned to client via response header that client echoes for retries. private deployments can opt-out but they'll get weaker guarantees.
Rachel: security note: tokens must be HMACed with per-cluster secret, or they can be forged and used to block/steal jobs. Can't expose cluster ids plain.
Jeff: hashing is fine. runtime signs token: base64(hmac(cluster_key, req_id|mode|ts)). verification is cheap. runtime still stays in control (no control-plane changes).
Miguel: rollout question — how to deploy without breaking older gateways/runtimes?
Anna (arch): backward compatible: if token missing, runtime behaves as today. If gateway cache enabled, it just reduces same-gateway retries. Token flow is opt-in via feature-flag per customer.
Rachel: add circuit-breaker: if gateway sees >X duplicate acceptances in window, slow down retries and route-through fallback queue to avoid overload.
Jeff: metrics to watch: duplicate_accept_count, gateway_cache_hit_ratio, cross_gateway_retries. Alert when duplicates > 0.1% of requests for 5m.
Miguel: I'll draft a short RFC with config shape + canary plan. Owners?
Anna (arch): Anna + Jeff for design, Miguel for rollout + config, Sara for private-compat/security signoff, Rachel for ops/runbook.
Sara: for private mode we should include an airgap appendix describing: local signing keys, no control-plane callbacks, and opt-out knob.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy started for gateway/lease-cache-feature on canary cluster c-42 :rocket:
Jeff: perf note — measure tail latency impact. local cache lookup should be O(1) but locking + LRU evictions must not block pipelined IO.
Rachel: I'll add the runbook steps: how to revert TTL, disable cache, and flush local caches if needed.
Miguel: thanks — I'll have first draft by EOD. +1 if you're ok with owners. :thumbsup:
Anna (arch): ack. thanks all.
Jeff: one more thought — for hosted->dedicated fallback, we might piggyback lease token in the routing header so dedicated runtime can short-circuit duplicate work if it sees the token already accepted. Will add to RFC.
Sara: and note in RFC that private-mode must never send cluster ids in plaintext; use hashed token only.
Rachel: cool. moving to RFC channel after draft. :v:
